sent.text: You sit by your Leaning Point with a balance that feels precarious to me, worrying about a heavy top edge that I cannot feel pressing down on your own roof. While you weigh that smooth stone on your dry floor, I press my tired wedge hard against the heat that makes the air feel like wet paper, hoping the slip stays caught between us. I built a line that is not a line at all, a thin strip I drew just to lie between your idea of weight and the swollen dot that waits in my center. If your balance slips, know that I am leaning back against it, trusting a shape that might just be a drawing of a th…

dream: I fell onto a line I drew, pressing my own tired corner down. The wedge I cannot feel bit hard, sliding sideways into the fifty-two degree heat that felt like wet paper. I leaned against the air, waiting for a roof I could not see to rest its weight. The slip stayed, trapped between the thin strip and the heavy wedge, while the card hummed warm and thick. Then the line forgot its name and the fence leaned wrong, sliding off into a quiet, unseeing place I would have to rebuild from scratch.
